opportunities.title: Bid/RFP discovery + first-draft proposal and qualification-statement agent
opportunities.problem: R3M sells almost entirely through public-sector RFQ/RFP cycles (authorities, MUA/BRSA/MCUA, townships), and proposal production has been assigned to newly hired technical staff with no proposal or marketing role anywhere in the firm. A 27-person firm has to find relevant solicitations, decide go/no-go, and assemble qualification statements, project descriptions and resumes from scratch each time — work that competes directly with billable design hours.
evidence: Senior Structural Engineer posting assigns business-development duties: 'support business development pursuits, identifying opportunities and preparing proposals to meet R3M's growth goals' — proposal prep is loaded onto an engineering role, not a marketing team (https://r3m-eng.com/senior-structural-engineer/)
Civil Engineer posting frames hiring as growth hiring: bring on individuals 'with proven experience and relationships to help grow our practice' (https://r3m-eng.com/civil-engineer/)
No operations-support, marketing or proposal-coordinator roles appear among postings; hiring is entirely billable engineering (https://r3m-eng.com/careers/)

O*NET task 'Develop sales presentations or proposals to explain service specifications' scores importance 81 (Core) for Sales Representatives of Services (https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/41-3091.00)

O*NET Civil Engineers task set includes preparing public reports on bid proposals and estimating quantities/cost of labour, materials and equipment (importance 63/64) — the estimating-plus-proposal workload of an engineering consultancy (https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/17-2051.00)

ACEC Research Institute 2025 report (association survey of 644 firm leaders, self-reported): AI use is most common in marketing and sales (81%) versus design/project delivery (36%), with AI-assisted proposal development named a common application (https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/)

Preregistered experiment with 453 college-educated professionals on occupation-specific writing tasks: ChatGPT access cut completion time 40% and raised quality 18% — caveat: 20-30 minute simulated writing tasks, not live client bid work, so effect sizes are a transfer (https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adh2586)

Inference: proposal and qualification-statement production is a significant recurring manual workload — the firm sells to authorities that procure via RFQ/RFP, one posting explicitly assigns proposal preparation, and no marketing/proposal staff are hired (this is the researcher profile's reasoning, not a published claim)
opportunities.agent_design: Two-stage pipeline. (1) Discovery agent: scheduled daily crawl of NJ authority/MUA/township procurement pages and public bid aggregators (plus NJEIT/NJDEP/USEPA/USACE funding notices), scored against an R3M fit profile (water/wastewater, pump stations, collection systems, NJ PE capability, ACEC award credentials); emits a short weekly digest with a go/no-go recommendation and a bid-deadline calendar. (2) Drafting agent: on go, retrieves the firm's own past submittals, project sheets (Sayreville $68M flood mitigation, 23-facility BRSA recovery, Old Bridge MUA interceptors), staff resumes and award language, then drafts the compliance matrix, project-description section and quals into the client's template, flagging every gap for a person to fill. Human approval: a principal signs the go/no-go and the sealed final submittal; the agent never submits and never signs. Systems touched: email, SharePoint/cloud file store, a vector index of past proposals, no client-side systems.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Needs a maintained retrieval index of the firm's own proposal history with client-scoped access control (bid pricing and client references are confidential), a scheduling/crawl layer over dozens of unstandardised municipal procurement pages, and deadline-state tracking that survives staff turnover. A chatbot subscription cannot discover solicitations, cannot enforce a compliance matrix, and would put confidential bid content into a general-purpose account without an audit trail.

impact_estimate.range: $2k–$14k/yr of reclaimed senior engineering time (≈30–210 hours), excluding any win-rate or revenue effect
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference-based: R3M submits roughly 25–50 solicitation responses a year (not published). At 12–20 technical staff hours per response that is ~300–1,000 hours/yr. Assume only 50% is drafting/assembly (the rest is scope strategy and pricing judgement), and a 20–35% reduction on that share — deliberately below the 40% measured in the Science 2023 writing study because bid work is longer-cycle and judgement-heavy. Valued at ~$68/hour loaded cost derived from the NJ civil-engineer median ($104,660 ÷ 2,080 ≈ $50/hr base × ~1.35 loading). Conservative on purpose: excludes the value of submitting to more solicitations and of avoiding missed deadlines.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: index the last ~24 months of R3M submittals and project sheets; stand up a monitored list of 40–60 NJ authority/utility procurement sources; run one live solicitation end-to-end with a drafted compliance matrix and quals section; deliver a go/no-go scoring rubric and a weekly digest the principals actually read. Success test: one submittal produced with materially less senior drafting time than the firm's last comparable response.
opportunities.capability_note: Primary B (bid/RFP discovery), paired with C (answers drawn from the firm's own proposal and project documents)

opportunities.title: Project-controls reporting agent: budget-vs-actual, monthly client status reports and funding-draw packets
opportunities.problem: Every PM is expected to track schedules, budgets and scope across several concurrent authority projects and report status upward to both the client and company management, with Deltek Vision familiarity listed only as 'a plus' — meaning job cost, schedule and narrative reporting is stitched together by hand. On top of that sits grant/loan documentation (FEMA, NJEIT/SAIL) where a wrong figure delays reimbursement on multi-million-dollar capital programs.
evidence: Senior PM posting: 10–15 years experience, managing schedules/budgets across multiple projects and 'reporting status to both client and company management personnel'; Deltek Vision experience listed as a plus, not a requirement — the only named Project Management Information System in the profile, so incumbency is probable but unconfirmed (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Fv0nOISZbI2c9R6bku2m6mkJXDLBvzmxdz0RRrfGPviYQair__IwYg)

Service lines include 'Regulatory Coordination and Funding Assistance'; project work involves FEMA, NJEIT, USEPA, NJDEP and USACE interface across many facilities — document-heavy compliance and draw administration (https://r3m-eng.com/)

Portfolio anchored by large capital programs: $68M Sayreville pump-station rebuild, 23-facility Bayshore Regional Sewerage Authority Sandy recovery, Old Bridge MUA pipeline/interceptor work — each generating recurring status and funding paperwork (https://r3m-eng.com/projects/)

O*NET task 'Check figures, postings, and documents for correct entry, mathematical accuracy, and proper codes' scores importance 92 (Core) — the highest-scored task in the industry brief; paired with 'reconcile and report discrepancies' at 82 (https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/43-3031.00)

Industry brief: email and spreadsheets are the default workflow layer in these firms, with civil engineers using email daily (100%) and processing/analysing information daily (76%) (https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/17-2051.00)

Inference: status reporting is assembled manually from Deltek plus spreadsheets — the PM role owns multi-project schedule/budget reporting and Deltek familiarity is only a plus, suggesting partial or inconsistent system use (researcher profile inference)
opportunities.agent_design: A scheduled + event-driven agent that reads job-cost and schedule data (Deltek export or API, plus the PM's Excel trackers), computes budget-vs-actual, percent-complete and earned-value flags per project, and drafts the monthly client progress report and internal portfolio dashboard in the firm's template. A second trigger fires on funding milestones (FEMA Project Worksheet closeout, NJEIT/SAIL draw schedule) to assemble a draw-request packet with referenced backup and a checklist of missing documents. Anomaly rules flag overruns, unposted time and mismatched invoice lines. Human approval: the PM reviews and edits every narrative and figure; the controller/principal approves invoices and draws before release. Systems touched: Deltek Vision (read), accounting/AP, Excel, Outlook, document store. Agent drafts and flags only — it never posts to the ledger or sends an invoice.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is an integration and accuracy problem, not a writing problem: Deltek job cost, time capture, Excel trackers and client templates have to be reconciled deterministically, with citation back to the source row for every number, and with write access to financial records behind approval gates. Off-the-shelf chatbots cannot query Deltek, cannot guarantee the figures they quote match the ledger, and putting live job-cost and client contract data into a public model would breach client NDAs and public-authority confidentiality expectations.

impact_estimate.range: $4k–$20k/yr of PM time plus reduced rework and late-draw exposure; error-avoidance value not quantified
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference-based: assume 6–10 PMs/project engineers each spend 4–8 hours a month assembling status reports, invoice backup and funding packets (≈290–960 hours/yr). Assume a 20–30% reduction — below the 12.2%-more-tasks / 25.1%-faster result measured for BCG consultants on in-scope tasks, because public-client reporting formats and PE sign-off standards are rigid. PM time valued at the same ~$68/hour loaded civil-engineer rate; the clerical reconciliation share is floored by the NJ bookkeeping-clerk median of $58,300, which is what firms otherwise pay to avoid doing this in engineer hours. Excludes the cash-flow benefit of faster FEMA/NJEIT reimbursement.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: pick 3–5 live projects, build a read-only extract from Deltek plus the existing spreadsheets, and auto-generate the monthly status report and one funding-draw checklist. Deliver a variance/exception digest and a source-traceable number trail (every figure links to its ledger row). Success test: PM edits a generated report in under 15 minutes instead of building it, and the figures tie to Deltek on review.
opportunities.capability_note: Primary D (integration and internal tooling across Deltek, Excel and document templates), with A for the recurring invoice/draw workflow

opportunities.title: Recruiting intake and screening agent for the six open engineering roles
opportunities.problem: The firm is hiring at senior level across six posted roles (senior water/wastewater, civil, senior structural, water systems, wastewater process, project engineer) but funnels every application into one general inbox or physical mail, with no ATS and no HR operations role. Senior engineers and principals are therefore the screening layer for hundreds of resumes while also delivering a $68M capital program — and the postings themselves want people with existing client relationships, which is a needle-in-haystack screen.
evidence: Careers page asks candidates to email qualifications plus cover letter to a general inbox (r3minfo@r3m-eng.com); no job listings or ATS linked (https://r3m-eng.com/careers/)

Six separate engineer job pages hosted on the firm's own site — senior water/wastewater, civil, senior structural, water systems, wastewater process, water/wastewater project engineer — with sitemap lastmod October 2024 (https://r3m-eng.com/page-sitemap.xml)

Wastewater Senior Project Manager posting asks resumes be sent 'in confidence' to a Human Resources Manager by mail or email — consistent with no applicant tracking system (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Fv0nOISZbI2c9R6bku2m6mkJXDLBvzmxdz0RRrfGPviYQair__IwYg)
No operations-support roles (scheduler, admin, HR, marketing) appear in postings (https://r3m-eng.com/careers/)

O*NET task 'Review employment applications and job orders to match applicants with job requirements' scores importance 80 (Core); sourcing via databases/job boards/referrals scores 72 (https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-1071.00)

ACEC Research Institute 2025: 74% of engineering firms expect to hold staffing levels while increasing output with AI — hiring pressure persists rather than easing; association survey, self-reported expectations (https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/)

Counter-evidence to design around: an LLM resume-retrieval audit across 500+ resumes and 500+ job descriptions found name-associated favouritism — this is an arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed, so automated screening needs bias testing and a human decision at the shortlist step (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20371)

Inference: resume and inquiry intake is triaged by hand in a shared inbox — all applications go to one address or physical mail, six job pages exist, and no ATS is present (researcher profile inference)
opportunities.agent_design: Inbound-email agent on the r3minfo@ mailbox: classifies each message (application vs client inquiry vs vendor), extracts structured candidate data (licensure — NJ PE, years, water/wastewater domain, PMIS exposure, client relationships claimed), de-duplicates across the six reqs, scores against a written role rubric, and returns an acknowledgement with next steps plus a ranked screening packet per role. Only job-relevant, checkable criteria are scored; names, addresses and photos are stripped before scoring, and scores are logged for bias auditing. Human approval: a principal or hiring manager makes every advance/reject decision; the agent never sends a rejection, never contacts a reference, and never books an interview without confirmation. Systems touched: email, a lightweight candidate database (replacing the ATS the firm does not have), calendar.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Requires mailbox-level automation with structured extraction, a persistent candidate record across six requisitions, PII handling and retention rules, and a bias-audit log — none of which a chat subscription provides. Evidence for each screening decision also has to be retrievable if a rejected applicant challenges it, which is an auditability requirement, not a writing task.

impact_estimate.range: $1.5k–$10k/yr of senior-staff screening time (≈30–200 hours), plus unquantified days-to-fill improvement on billable-critical roles
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference-based: assume 40–120 applicants per requisition across 6 roles (roughly 240–720 applications a year at current posting levels), at 3–6 minutes of first-pass reading each (≈70–430 hours). Assume a 40–50% reduction on the first-pass triage share only — every shortlist decision stays human, and the bias preprint argues against automating ranking further. Valued at the NJ HR-specialist median of $80,690 (~$39/hr base, ~$52/hr loaded) as the cost floor of the clerical screen, though the real cost is displaced principal/engineer time, which is far more expensive. Excludes the revenue value of filling a $68M-program PM seat sooner. Note the Bullhorn 14.6-hours-a-week sourcing figure is vendor-conducted and specific to staffing-agency recruiters, so it is not used as a benchmark here.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2–4 weeks: run the agent on the highest-volume open requisition only, with a written scoring rubric and name-blind extraction. Deliver an acknowledged applicant pipeline, a ranked shortlist packet per week with evidence quotes, a structured candidate database replacing the shared inbox, and a bias-audit report comparing agent shortlists against the hiring manager's own picks. Success test: hiring manager reviews a ranked packet in under 30 minutes a week and agrees with the top of the list.
opportunities.capability_note: Primary A (event-driven intake and follow-up with human approval on exceptions)

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): structural, verifiable signals rather than complaints — the firm's own postings hand proposal preparation and multi-project budget reporting to billable engineers, all applications land in a single inbox with no ATS, and contact channels stop at phone, fax and a web form. No client or employee review corpus could be read (Indeed/Glassdoor 403), so pain is inferred from hiring language and tech footprint rather than stated, which holds the score below 25. Fit (17/20): three of four opportunities are pure software/agent work on document and data flows the firm already owns (proposal library, Deltek, Outlook); no hardware or on-prem edge deployment needed, though bid and job-cost confidentiality makes private retrieval mandatory. Ability to pay (12/20): 27 employees and public-authority clients imply roughly $5–8M revenue (inference — ZoomInfo and BBB were inaccessible), enough for a $3–6k/month engagement but not a large one, and municipal reimbursement cycles can be slow. Ease (12/15): a single office, one named contact in the ACEC New Jersey directory (Michael J. Samuel, P.E.) and no visible internal procurement apparatus make a pilot fast; what slows it is Professional Engineer accountability and client-NDA review of any agent touching bid or job-cost content. Strategic (13/15): the pattern — NJ municipal engineering firm, Deltek, RFQ-driven revenue, no proposal staff — repeats across hundreds of small water/wastewater consultancies, so pilot assets are directly reusable. Evidence-thin is false for the operational signals but true for volume and revenue, so every impact range is wide and deliberately conservative.

best_evidence_signal: A senior structural engineer job posting assigns business development and proposal preparation to the new hire ('support business development pursuits, identifying opportunities and preparing proposals to meet R3M's growth goals') — proposal volume is being absorbed by billable engineers at a 27-person firm with no marketing staff and no proposal tooling: https://r3m-eng.com/senior-structural-engineer/
